claim.markdown_says: ## 14.9.22.4 General rules [specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27892 - level 2, the same rank as '## 14.9.22 INSPECT statement' at line 27762, whereas the directly comparable '### 14.9.21.4 General rules' at line 27735 is correctly level 3 under '## 14.9.21 INITIATE statement']
claim.why_it_matters: At level 2 the General rules of INSPECT are a sibling of the INSPECT statement section rather than its child, so a heading-derived outline shows 14.9.22.4 detached from 14.9.22 and shows 14.9.22 as containing only General/General formats/Syntax rules. The neighbouring INITIATE section proves the intended level is 3, so this is an internal inconsistency, not a transcription convention.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The rendered PDF page 675 (printed folio 645) carries exactly one heading, set in bold: '14.9.22.4 General rules', sitting between General rule 9) of the Syntax rules ('When both literal-4 and literal-5 are specified they shall be the same size except when literal-5 is a figurative constant.') and the 'ALL FORMATS' banner that precedes General rule 1). The markdown at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27895 reads '## 14.9.22.4 General rules', preceded by its anchor '' at line 27894, in precisely that position and order. The heading text, its section number, and its placement are transcribed verbatim and correctly. The claim's own kind, 'missing-heading', is therefore a misnomer for what is at most a heading-DEPTH difference. (2) THE DIFFERENCE IS PURE TRANSCRIPTION FORMATTING WITH NO PDF COUNTERPART. A markdown '#' count is an attribute of the transcription, not of the source: the PDF expresses hierarchy typographically and, decisively, through the dotted section number itself. The number '14.9.22.4' is present and intact, and it states the parentage unambiguously and machine-readably. No normative content, no syntax rule, no general rule, no operand name, no semantics differs between the two documents on this page. (3) THE CLAIM'S CENTRAL JUSTIFICATION IS EMPIRICALLY FALSE. The claim asserts 'this is an internal inconsistency, not a transcription convention.' Measured over the whole file: 162 four-part (N.N.N.N) headings are at level 2, 620 at level 3, 24 at level 4 - so the level-2 form is roughly 20% of all such headings, not a one-off. Sampling 60 of each and locating the nearest preceding parent heading shows what actually drives it: 55/60 (92%) of the LEVEL-2 four-part headings are separated from their parent heading by at least one intervening '## Page NNN' break, versus only 6/60 (10%) of the LEVEL-3 ones. The depth demotion is a systematic artifact of the page-at-a-time transcription pipeline, which resets heading depth at a page boundary. This case fits the pattern exactly: '## 14.9.22 INSPECT statement' is on page 673, while 14.9.22.3 and 14.9.22.4 fall on pages 674 and 675. The contrasting INITIATE example proves nothing about intent - 14.9.21 and all four of its children (14.9.21.1 through 14.9.21.4, lines 27716-27738) sit together on page 672 with no page break between them, which is why they retained level 3. The claim mistook a page-break artifact for a semantic inconsistency. (4) THE CLAIM MISQUOTES THE MARKDOWN. It states the outline 'shows 14.9.22 as containing only General/General formats/Syntax rules', i.e. it presumes 14.9.22.3 Syntax rules is a properly-nested child. It is not: '## 14.9.22.3 Syntax rules' at line 27856 is ALSO at level 2, demoted by the same page-673-to-674 break. The claim singles out .4 while overlooking .3 on the very same statement, so its stated consequence is inaccurate. Its three cited line numbers are each 3 too low as well: 14.9.22.4 is at 27895 (not 27892), '## 14.9.22 INSPECT statement' at 27765 (not 27762), '### 14.9.21.4 General rules' at 27738 (not 27735). Per the rejection criteria this is page-break furniture plus formatting, the allegedly missing text is present, the meaning is unchanged, and the claim misquotes the markdown. If the heading-depth normalization is ever wanted, it is a global mechanical pass over ~162 headings driven by the section-number arity, not a page-675 spec-reconciliation finding.
verdict.corrected_description: No discrepancy. The heading '14.9.22.4   General rules' printed on PDF page 675 is transcribed verbatim and in the correct position at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27895. The only difference is the markdown heading depth ('##' rather than '###'), a transcription-pipeline artifact that demotes any subsection separated from its parent by a page break - 92% of the file's 162 level-2 four-part headings show this signature, including '## 14.9.22.3 Syntax rules' at line 27856, which the claim overlooked. No spec content, hierarchy information (the number 14.9.22.4 is intact), or meaning is lost.
